title: 2023 AMC 12B Problem 18
statement: Last academic year Yolanda and Zelda took different courses that did not necessarily administer the same number of quizzes during each of the two semesters. Yolanda’s average on all the quizzes she took during the first semester was \(3\) points higher than Zelda’s average on all the quizzes she took during the first semester. Yolanda’s average on all the quizzes she took during the second semester was \(18\) points higher than her average for the first semester and was again \(3\) points higher than Zelda’s average on all the quizzes Zelda took during her second semester. Which one of the following statements cannot possibly be true?

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text:
Yolanda’s quiz average for the academic year
was \(22\) points higher than Zelda’s.

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text:
Zelda’s quiz average for the academic year was higher than
Yolanda’s.

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text:
Yolanda’s quiz average for the academic year was \(3\) points
higher than Zelda’s.

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text:
Zelda’s quiz average for the academic year equaled
Yolanda’s.

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text:
If Zelda had scored \(3\) points higher on each quiz she took,
then she would have had the same average for the academic year as
Yolanda.

solutions.text:
Subtracting Zelda’s first-semester average from all four semester averages does not affect the comparison. We may therefore write the semester averages as \(0,18\) for Zelda and \(3,21\) for Yolanda. Let \(p\) and \(q\) be the fractions of Yolanda’s and Zelda’s quizzes, respectively, that occurred in the second semester. Their yearly-average difference is \[ (3+18p)-18q=3+18(p-q). \] Because \(0\lt p,q\lt 1,\) this difference is less than \(21,\) so it cannot be \(22.\)

The other options really can occur. Taking \((p,q)=(\tfrac14,\tfrac34)\) makes Zelda’s average higher; taking \(p=q\) makes Yolanda’s average \(3\) points higher (and also verifies the last option after adding \(3\) to every Zelda score); and taking \((p,q)=(\tfrac13,\tfrac12)\) makes the yearly averages equal. Each displayed fraction can be realized by positive integer quiz counts.

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Let Zelda’s first-semester average be \(0,\) and write the other three semester averages using the given gaps
If \(p,q\) are the fractions of Yolanda’s and Zelda’s quizzes taken in semester two, their yearly-average difference is \(3+18(p-q)\)
